subject: Pool prioritization matrix and temporary autoscale signal
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q4 sprint — temporary pool prioritization ask

Kim —

Quick heads up: HealthLytics is moving a hard demo + loadtest into our Q4 sprint (week of 10/12). They need consistent low-p99 latency for an analytics demo and we agreed to provide a short burst lane and higher concurrency for five days. Product would like a prioritized slice for the demo window rather than the usual best-effort queueing.

I attached a first-pass priority matrix (high/medium/low routes) and the expected throughput curve. Can infra temporarily relax auto-eviction for that slice and bump the concurrency cap by 2x for the window? We know this will increase token cost but it’s a strategic pilot — HealthLytics is on a fast renewal path if demo goes well.

Can you loop in Marcus and Neha and confirm what we need for approvals and what the ops constraints would be?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[attachment: pool-priority-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 sprint — temporary pool prioritization ask

Thanks, Laura — I reviewed the matrix. High-level thoughts before we dig into the numbers:

- We can create a temporary priority band for HealthLytics, but we need an explicit autoscale "signal" window and two operational guardrails: a maximum share of the pool (30%) and a pre-agreed rollback trigger (node pressure > 85% for 15m).
- Marcus will confirm whether that 2x concurrency fits the current slice topology; if not, we’ll need a short config change and a canary rollout.
- We need sign-off from Finance for the one-off surcharge and an ops runbook for the rollback.

Marcus / Neha — please advise on implementation steps and whether the rollback trigger above is reasonable. Laura — please send a one-paragraph business justification I can attach to the finance request.

-kim
Kimberly Park

Quick ops note after looking at current topology:

- The 2x concurrency bump is doable if we pin HealthLytics routes to a soft slice with CPU/GPU reservations (we’ll use a soft quota to avoid hard fragmentation).
- Implementation steps: 1) create slice config change (canary 5% traffic), 2) monitor KV cache hit and p99 latency for 1 hour, 3) roll to 100% of the slice, 4) enable signal window with the rollback trigger Kim suggested.
- I drafted an ops-runbook with the exact CLI commands and the rollback playbook. Attaching here.
- One constraint: we need to coordinate a temporary autoscaler override on the infra provider side for 10/12–10/16 (we don’t have spare node buffer in the us-west-2 pool that week).

I’ll open JIRA INF-4321 to track the slice change and link the runbook.

—Marcus

Date: 2026-10-02T08:11:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary autoscaler signal window for us-west-2 (2026-10-12 to 10-16)

Hi Alex —

Hope you’re well. We need a temporary autoscaler "signal" window for our Redwood-us-west-2 GPU pool from 2026-10-12 00:00 UTC through 2026-10-16 23:59 UTC. The ask: allow a soft capacity top-up (up to 30% of the pool) for a named slice (HealthLytics-demo) and suppress preemptive eviction for that slice unless node pressure exceeds 85% for 15 consecutive minutes (rollback on that trigger).

We will supply the canary plan and runbook (JIRA INF-4321) and will coordinate a pre-window smoke test on 10/11. This is a one-time commercial pilot tied to a customer demo; Finance has provisionally approved a surcharge pending your confirmation of feasibility.

Please confirm whether you can: 1) enable the signal window, 2) apply the soft quota cap, and 3) provide any provider-side constraints we should be aware of.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Capacity & Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Reed <sre.ops@acmecloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary autoscaler signal window for us-west-2 (2026-10-12 to 10-16)

Kim —

We can support the requested signal window with the following caveats:

- We can provision additional nodes to satisfy the 30% soft top-up for those dates but need a firm headcount estimate by 2026-10-05 so we can lock capacity.
- The provider autoscaler cannot suppress eviction entirely; we can implement a suppression *policy* that biases against preemption for the named slice until node pressure > 80% for 10m. We can match your 85%/15m trigger as a secondary check but primary enforcement is 80%/10m on our side (we recommend keeping both monitors).
- There will be a short lead time to change the eviction policy (2 business days).
- If pressure approaches critical, we will send an automated escalation to your oncall and to Finance to expedite any emergency top-ups.

To proceed we need: 1) the pool headcount estimate (expected concurrent jobs), 2) the slice identifier you will use (HealthLytics-demo), and 3) a signed change-affecting-ops doc (we can accept a PDF).

If you can get the info by 10/05, we’ll schedule the node changes and policy overlay.

—Alex Reed
SRE Ops, AcmeCloud
[attachment: autoscale-signal-request.pdf (pdf)]
